definition: Veneer means a superficial or deceptively attractive appearance, facade.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word veneer. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know veneer should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Fresh sod gave the abandoned mine's entrance a veneer of parkland.
A sheen is only a surface impression — it stops short of a veneer, which is a false layer deliberately laid on.
A charade goes further than a veneer: not a thin covering over the truth but a whole performance in place of it.

A gloss is a thin shine of respectability brushed over something — a quick coat that improves how it reads without changing what it is. A veneer is more constructed: a whole false surface deliberately laid on to hide a different reality. A press release puts a gloss on bad news; staged charity builds a veneer of virtue.

A front is the false outward show a person performs — the brave face, the respectable act kept up for an audience. A veneer keeps the carpentry image: a thin attractive layer applied onto a thing, a business, or a life. People put up fronts; buildings and reputations wear veneers.

A front is what a person performs; a gloss is shallower still; veneer keeps the carpentry image of a layer glued on.
